'''Shelley Hurwitz''' is an American [[biostatistics|biostatistician]]. She is the Director of Biostatistics in the Center for Clinical Investigation at [[Brigham and Women's Hospital]],{{r|bwh}} and an associate professor in the [[Harvard Medical School]].{{r|biosketch}}

==Ethics==
As well as biostatistics, Hurwitz maintains an interest in [[Applied ethics|professional ethics]] for statisticians. She chaired the Committee on Professional Ethics of the [[American Statistical Association]] from 2010 to 2012,{{r|jsm|catalyst}} chaired the Committee on Ethical Practice of Clinical and Translational Biostatistics of the [[Clinical and Translational Science Award|CTSA Consortium]] from 2012 to 2014,{{r|catalyst}} and belongs to the Advisory Board on Ethics of the [[International Statistical Institute]].{{r|isi-ethics}}

==Education and career==
Hurwitz has two master's degrees: an M.A. in psychology from [[Arizona State University]], earned in 1977,
and an M.S. in statistics from [[Stanford University]], earned in 1981.
She completed her Ph.D. in psychology in 1992 at [[Temple University]].{{r|biosketch}} Her dissertation was ''Judgments of Correlation: Level of Measurement and Co-occurrence Bias''.{{r|catalyst}}
She worked as a statistician at the [[University of Pennsylvania]] from 1981 to 1992, when she moved to the [[Harvard School of Public Health]].
In 1997, she moved again, to Brigham and Women's Hospital, and at the same time took a teaching position in the [[Harvard Medical School]]. She became a regular-rank faculty member at Harvard in 2005.{{r|biosketch}}

==Recognition==
In 2011, Hurwitz was elected to the International Statistical Institute.{{r|isi-members}}
In 2014, she became a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].{{r|fasa}}
